# llms-full.txt

## Project summary

StealthEye Agent OS is a foundation for broad delegated autonomy: authorized online-task agents operating through ChatGPT custom apps/MCP, durable workers, Mission OS, app-host surfaces, mission-scoped authority, signed manifests, Guard decisions, CodeOps, CI Repair, evals, receipts, replayable evidence, Memory Graph context, and compliance-ready controls. This public repo contains non-sensitive architecture, specs, governance, scaffolding, eval templates, generated build state, and compliance planning only.

## Current build state

Build 1 established the public-visible, locked-down repo posture, baseline docs, branch/PR workflow, public/private boundary, and no-secrets foundation for later packages.

Build 2 adds `@stealtheye/agent-registry`: signed agent/tool manifests, JSON Schema export, deterministic canonicalization, SHA-256 digesting, Ed25519 signing/verification helpers, risk-relevant diffing, in-memory trust registry, revocation lists, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 3 adds `@stealtheye/guard`: capability-token schemas, requested actions, Guard decisions/receipts, lifecycle helpers, deterministic token/action matching, hard-stop evaluation, registry trust checks, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 4 adds `@stealtheye/mission-os`: StealthEye Mission Language, normalized mission schemas, authority envelopes, lightweight mission plans, status snapshots, receipt references, compiler outputs for Guard capability-token templates and requested actions, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 5 adds `@stealtheye/app-host`: app metadata, MCP-style preview tool descriptors, input/output schemas, resource descriptors, fixture-backed handlers, and Vitest eval-style tests for host, mission, Guard, registry, and policy tool families. All Build 5 tools are read-only, fixture-only, or preview-only.

Build 6 adds `@stealtheye/worker-fleet`: typed worker task schemas, task types/statuses, lease schemas with fencing tokens, idempotency records and stable action fingerprints, retry policy/state helpers, task status summaries, artifact references, worker receipt events, Guard preflight helpers, Mission OS plan-to-worker-task conversion, fixtures, and Vitest eval-style tests.

Build 7 adds `@stealtheye/codeops`: CodeOps + CI Repair schemas, repository targets, branch/path safety helpers, patch plans, file-change contracts, verification plans, CI log summaries/classifiers, repair plans, rerun eligibility policy, PR evidence packets, Guard requested-action adapters, Worker Fleet task templates, fixtures, and Vitest eval-style tests. It is foundation-only and does not perform live GitHub mutation or CI reruns.

Build 8 adds `@stealtheye/browserops`: fixture-only browser sessions, page observations, evidence refs, action policies, action plans, Guard preflight, Worker Fleet task templates, public-safe fixtures, generated build state, and marker-bounded hand-authored doc preservation. It does not add Playwright runtime execution, credentialed browsing, live website interaction, material external sends, purchases/payments, destructive actions, production mutation, or private infrastructure.

Build 9 adds `@stealtheye/receipts-replay`: receipt event schemas, evidence refs, receipt bundles, mission timeline helpers, descriptive replay packets, verification packets, final report packets, deterministic integrity digests, adapters from existing subsystem fixtures, and generated build state. It is foundation-only and does not add durable ledger storage, production artifact storage, live replay execution, live tool execution, real browser execution, live CodeOps mutation, CI reruns, production mutation, money movement, secrets, customer data, or private infrastructure.

Build 10 adds `@stealtheye/mcp-runtime`: a local/dev in-process MCP-style runtime wrapper around the safe App Host tool surface. It adds runtime metadata, health/capabilities, tool listing/calls, resource listing/reads, dev-mode connection information, transport-style request handling, and public-safe receipt previews. It does not add an official hosted MCP transport, public app submission, live writes, worker execution, durable receipt storage, browser execution, credentialed browsing, repo mutation, deployment, money movement, customer workflows, or production readiness.

Build 11 adds `@stealtheye/repo-status`: Guard-gated public GitHub repository/status observation plus read-only repo/status tools in `@stealtheye/mcp-runtime`. It models public repo metadata, branch metadata, PR/issue metadata, workflow/check summaries, public-safe file metadata/content, read policy, Guard adapter decisions, receipt previews, fixture clients, and an optional unauthenticated public REST client constrained to GET requests against `https://api.github.com` for an explicit public repository allowlist. It does not add private repo access, credentials, branch creation, commits, PR/issue mutation, CI reruns, workflow dispatch, deployment, browser execution, money movement, production mutation, or customer workflows.

Build 12 adds `@stealtheye/memory-graph`: fixture-only, deterministic, in-memory Memory Graph schemas, helpers, fixtures, tests, generated-state declarations, and preview-only runtime tools. It defines typed memory nodes and edges, provenance/source references, evidence and receipt refs, confidence, recency, retention hints, query helpers, compaction helpers, retention reports, public-safe context summaries, receipt previews, generated build-state refs, and fixture-backed conceptual integration with Mission OS, Receipts + Replay, Repo Status, MCP Runtime, and build automation. It does not add a production database, vector database, embeddings provider, cloud storage, private knowledge ingestion, durable personal memory, live memory service, live writes, production mutation, or secret storage.

## Architecture overview

The default stack is TypeScript monorepo, Node.js MCP servers, Postgres for durable mission/control/evidence state, Redis + BullMQ for initial worker queues, Temporal as future workflow orchestration, S3/R2-compatible artifact storage, GitHub App auth, Playwright BrowserOps, OpenAI Responses API + Apps SDK integration, and Zod + JSON Schema for mission/tool/workflow/receipt/authority/agent-card/worker/codeops/memory schemas.

Key systems: Mission OS, App Host, Agent Registry, Guard, Capability Tokens, Worker Fleet, CodeOps, CI Repair, BrowserOps, Receipts + Replay, MCP Runtime, Repo Status, Memory Graph, Evals, Workflow Compiler, Semantic Firewall, A2A Subagent Network, Agent Arena, StagingOps/Observability, and domain ops apps.

## App Host model

App Host is the first ChatGPT App / MCP Server Host Shell foundation. It models tool/resource descriptors and fixture-backed handlers that can later be wired to an official MCP or ChatGPT Apps runtime. Build 5 does not expose live repo mutation, worker execution, browser automation, deployments, money movement, customer data, remote trust discovery, or production-grade credential flows. Builds 10 through 12 expose App Host capabilities through the local/dev runtime without changing the App Host safety contract.

## Mission OS model

Mission OS converts broad goals into typed Mission Language, normalized mission objects, authority envelopes, plan/DAG structures, status summaries, receipt references, and Guard-compatible requested actions. Build 6 Worker Fleet consumes Mission OS plans and preserves mission, plan, step, dependency, receipt, capability-token, and requested-action context when creating worker tasks. Build 7 CodeOps patch plans can be associated with mission and task IDs for future mission-to-code handoff. Build 12 Memory Graph can model mission/task nodes and context packets from fixture-only graph bundles.

## Worker Fleet model

Worker Fleet is the durable execution substrate contract for future mission-step execution. Build 6 defines package-level schemas and deterministic helpers for worker tasks, leases, idempotency, retries, status transitions, summaries, artifacts, receipts, Guard preflight, and Mission OS handoff. Build 7 CodeOps creates Worker Fleet task templates for future CodeOps and CI Repair steps without executing live actions. Build 9 can convert Worker Fleet receipt event fixtures into Receipts + Replay receipt events for replay packets.

## CodeOps and CI Repair model

CodeOps owns branch-safe repository operation contracts: repo targets, branch-prefix rules, protected branch detection, path allow/deny matching, patch plans, file-change contracts, verification plans, PR evidence, and Guard/Worker Fleet preflight adapters. CI Repair owns CI/check summary interpretation, deterministic fixture-log classification, repair planning, rerun eligibility, and verification loop contracts.

Both are foundation-only in Build 7. There is no live branch creation, commit write, PR creation, log scraping, workflow dispatch, failed-job rerun, protected branch mutation, force push, CI weakening, deployment, secret access, or customer-data mutation. Build 9 records CodeOps and CI Repair evidence as public-safe receipt refs; it does not perform live repo or CI actions.

## BrowserOps model

BrowserOps is the future browser/computer-use layer for authorized online workflows. Build 8 provides fixture-only contracts for sessions, observations, evidence references, action policies, action plans, Guard preflight, and Worker Fleet handoff templates. Build 9 can record BrowserOps preflight summaries and browser evidence references as receipt events and replay steps, but it still does not execute browsers or capture real browser artifacts.

## Receipts + Replay model

Receipts + Replay reconstructs what happened from public-safe references. Build 9 captures event order, subsystem summaries, evidence refs, artifact refs, denials/escalations, verification checks, final reports, and integrity digests. Replay packets are descriptive and side-effect-free: they do not execute tools, call APIs, rerun CI, launch browsers, mutate state, access secrets, or touch production/customer data. Build 12 Memory Graph preserves provenance, evidence refs, and receipt refs without adding a durable ledger.

## MCP Runtime and Repo Status model

MCP Runtime is the local/dev runtime wrapper for safe tool descriptors, tool calls, resources, receipt previews, and runtime metadata. Build 10 wraps App Host tools. Build 11 adds read-only public repo/status tools. Build 12 adds fixture-only Memory Graph preview tools. Runtime tools must remain read-only or preview/fixture-only, with no live writes, destructive effects, credentialed access, workflow dispatch, CI reruns, or production mutation.

Repo Status models public repository observation only. It keeps read policy, Guard decisions, public-safe receipt previews, fixture clients, and optional unauthenticated public GitHub reads separate from any future write path.

## Memory Graph model

Memory Graph is the durable-knowledge model foundation, but Build 12 is deliberately storage-free. It models nodes such as mission, task, agent, tool, repo, branch, pull_request, issue, workflow_run, file, receipt_event, evidence_ref, build, decision, capability, policy, gap, fact, and summary. It models edges such as derived_from, supports, contradicts, supersedes, references, produced_by, verified_by, blocked_by, depends_on, belongs_to, related_to, summarizes, observed_in, and governed_by.

Build 12 Memory Graph helpers validate graph bundles, retrieve nodes, list nodes by type, list edges, find connected nodes, search by tag/text, filter by source type/confidence/sensitivity, produce mission/task context packets, produce public-safe summaries, compact related summary nodes, detect stale or superseded facts, and produce retention reports. It keeps provenance and receipt references through compaction and retention reporting and does not delete anything.

## Agent Registry and Guard model

Signed payloads are verified over canonical unsigned payloads. Guard consumes registry trust summaries and enforces capability-token constraints, pinned digests, hard stops, lifecycle state, and mission-scoped target/effect boundaries.

Capability tokens are delegated-authority records. Authority envelopes produced by Mission OS are templates/structures that can later feed Guard-capability issuance. Worker Fleet calls Guard preflight for action-bearing tasks and records receipt/status suggestions without executing actions. Build 7 CodeOps produces Guard requested actions for future repo/CI operations and blocks hard-stop paths before execution exists. Build 9 records Guard decisions as receipt events and final-report evidence.

## Mission/build workflow

1. Jamie opens a new ChatGPT tab for the next build prompt.
2. Builder completes focused repo work on a branch.
3. Builder updates docs, AGENTS.md, llms files, eval expectations, receipt/evidence expectations, and verification checklist where applicable.
4. Jamie returns to verifier chat with PR/branch/commit.
5. Verifier checks implementation against issue #1 and docs.
6. Verifier merges accepted green PRs and updates issue #1.
7. Verifier provides the next prompt.

## Docs map

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: system components and data/control flow.
- `docs/AUTONOMY_MODEL.md`: authority, autonomy, and hard stops.
- `docs/CODEOPS.md`: Build 7 branch-safe CodeOps contracts and boundaries.
- `docs/CI_REPAIR.md`: Build 7 CI classification, repair planning, rerun policy, and boundaries.
- `docs/WORKER_FLEET.md`: task, lease, idempotency, retry, receipt, artifact, Guard preflight, Mission OS handoff, and CodeOps task-template relationship.
- `docs/APP_HOST.md`: Build 5 app-host tool/resource surface and boundaries.
- `docs/MISSION_OS.md`: Mission Language, mission schemas, compiler, status, receipts, Guard integration, Worker Fleet handoff, and future CodeOps handoff.
- `docs/CUSTOM_APPS.md`: app inventory and responsibilities.
- `docs/AGENT_REGISTRY.md`: signed cards/manifests, trust, revocation, Guard integration assumptions.
- `docs/SECURITY.md`: MCP/OAuth/security boundaries, Worker Fleet, CodeOps, Repo Status, Memory Graph boundaries, and hard stops.
- `docs/WORKFLOWS.md`: mission lifecycle, worker handoff, CodeOps/CI Repair loops, DAGs, retries, idempotency, and replay workflow.
- `docs/EVALS.md`: eval philosophy and suites.
- `docs/RECEIPTS.md`, `docs/REPLAY.md`, and `docs/EVIDENCE_MODEL.md`: evidence and replay.
- `docs/MCP_RUNTIME.md`: local/dev runtime surface, safe tools, repo/status tools, and Memory Graph preview tools.
- `docs/REPO_STATUS.md`: public repo/status read-only boundary.
- `docs/MEMORY_GRAPH.md`: Build 12 Memory Graph foundation model.
- `docs/BUILD_AUTOMATION.md`: generated build-state, strict generated sync, and marker-bounded doc preservation behavior.
- Compliance/security/governance docs map controls to readiness, not certification.

## Compliance and evidence summary

The project intends to align evidence with NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act readiness, ISO/IEC 42001 readiness, NIST CSF 2.0, NIST SSDF, OWASP LLM/Agentic threats, SOC 2 readiness, ISO 27001/27002/27701 readiness, GDPR/CCPA readiness, SLSA/SBOM/provenance, and sector-triggered frameworks. No certification is claimed.

## Public/private boundary

Public: architecture, public specs, non-sensitive schemas, app/tool scaffolding, worker-fleet contracts, CodeOps/CI Repair contracts, BrowserOps contracts, Receipts + Replay contracts, MCP Runtime local/dev contracts, Repo Status public-read contracts, Memory Graph fixture-only contracts, generated build state, examples/mock data, eval templates, governance and compliance docs. Private: sensitive operational material, production infrastructure, customer data, deployed runtime configuration, production receipt ledgers, artifact storage credentials, durable memory storage, and internal accounts.

